references.text: Abram passed through the land to the place near Shechem, to the oak of Moreh. At that time the Canaanites were in the land.

Jacob made a vow and said: 'If God is with me and keeps me on this journey I am taking, and gives me bread to eat and clothing to wear, and if I return safely to my father's house, then the Lord shall be my God.'
Dinah, the daughter whom Leah had borne to Jacob, went out to visit the women of the land. Shechem, son of the Hivite Hamor, who was the ruler of that place, saw her.
They gave Jacob all the foreign gods they had and the rings that were in their ears. Jacob buried them under the oak tree near Shechem.

The bones of Joseph, which the Israelites had brought up from Egypt, were buried at Shechem in the plot of land that Jacob had bought from the sons of Hamor, Shechem's father, for a hundred kesitahs. It became an inheritance for Joseph's descendants.
He came to a city in Samaria called Sychar, near the field that Jacob had given to his son Joseph.
Both verses document different phases of Jacob's return to Canaan after Paddan-Aram; 33:18 shows the physical arrival and encampment, while 35:9 confirms the spiritual blessing that follows.
37:1 confirms and summarizes the settlement that began with the arrival in 33:18; both verses mark the transition from 'foreigner' to 'settled' in Canaan.
Both verses describe phases of Jacob's arrival in Canaan; together they outline his route through Bethel and onward to Shechem.
